correctness.rationale: Prime-power bounds from exact alternating sums and multiplicativity give all quotient restrictions. Odd cases and odd-prime powers have quotient strictly between one and two. For even two-support integers, the odd prime exponent must be even; elementary inequalities reduce the final case to 3^(b+1)−2^(a+1)=5, contradicted mod 8. All boundary exceptions are explicitly evaluated. Verified code independently computes 2..50000; finite tests are corroboration only.
